before: lang identifies the language of an element and its descendants unless a descendant overrides it. A short passage in another language can carry its own lang. This helps tools interpret the content; it does not translate the words.

dir controls text direction: ltr, rtl or auto. It is not a language code. bdi isolates a piece of bidirectional text so its direction does not unintentionally affect surrounding text. dir="auto" lets direction be determined from that isolated text, useful for names supplied by different people.

before.question: You set lang="fr" on only the greeting span inside an English main. What happens to the surrounding English text?
choices: The entire document automatically becomes French.
It keeps the inherited English language; only the span overrides it.
Every word is translated into French.
before.explanation: A descendant language attribute overrides its own subtree, not its ancestors or neighboring content.

after.question: Only a greeting span has lang="fr" inside an English main. What language is marked for the words around it?
choices: French, because the span changes the whole page.
English. The change applies only inside the span.
The browser translates every word into French.
after.explanation: The span’s language setting applies to its own contents. The surrounding text keeps the main element’s English setting.
